summary: Roots reggae: 65-85 BPM one drop (kick and rim together on 3, swung hats), a deep round melodic bass as the loudest part, off-beat skank chords on guitar with an organ bubble, two-chord vamps, echo and spring reverb; knowledge/style/reggae.json is its template
body: Tempo: 60-90 BPM, usually 70-80; laid back, the pocket slightly behind the beat.

Drums: the one drop: nothing on 1, kick and rim (sidestick) together on 3, hi-hats in swung 8ths with an open hat into the next bar; a rim or snare fill only at the end of 4 or 8 bars, crash rare; rockers adds kicks on 1 and 3, steppers a kick on every beat; a dry live kit through a spring reverb.

Bass: deep, round, low-passed (treble and upper mids rolled off), loud and melodic: the loudest part, locked with the kick, on the strong beats with syncopated pickups and space between notes; a P-bass played with the fingers.

Harmony: two- or four-chord vamps, i-iv, I-IV, I-ii, I-IV-V; the skank: short chord stabs on every off-beat ('and'), on a clean guitar (or piano), often echoed; an organ bubble (shuffled 16ths around the off-beat) under it; a held chord pattern should be shortened to off-beat stabs.
Lead: a sparse melodica, organ or horn line (Augustus Pablo, Jackie Mittoo), mixed low; the template uses a harmonica as the melodica.
Texture/master: warm and bass-heavy, top end soft; tape or spring echo on the rim and skank, dub throws optional; never bright or squashed.

Sources (2026-11-26): MusicRadar 'How to program a typical one drop reggae beat and add fills'; Wayne and Wax 'Feel It In The One-Drop: A Roots Riddims Tutorial'; SoundFingers 'In the dub studio: 10 essential reggae music production tips'; Sound On Sound 'Dub mixing'.
Apply: pattern/one-drop on the drums, then pattern/prog-reggae-characteristic-1 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/reggae.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
